\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ} (phisalṇā)}{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ (phisalṇā)}]{\pa{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ} (phisalṇā) — to slip}

\label{lesson:PA-C310-phisalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a din, then the Punjabi for to die.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ}} — \emph{phisalṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to slip\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਕੱਲ੍ਹ} \pa{ਮੀਂਹ} \pa{ਵਿੱਚ} \pa{ਅਮਨ} \pa{ਸੜਕ} \pa{ਉੱਤੇ} \pa{ਫਿਸਲਿਆ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kall mīṁh vich Aman saṛak utte phisliā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Yesterday Aman slipped on the road in the rain.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਪੌੜੀ} \pa{ਉੱਤੇ} \pa{ਫਿਸਲਿਆ}, \emph{maiṁ pauṛī utte phisliā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ}} (\emph{phisalṇā}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*phiss}, \textquotedblleft{}slip\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{phisalṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to slip\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 9080).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phisalṇā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phisalṇā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kall mīṁh vich Aman saṛak utte phisliā.} — Yesterday Aman slipped on the road in the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for a din, then the Punjabi for to die, then say \emph{phisalṇā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਫਿਸਲਣਾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To slip\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਠੋਕਰ} (ṭhokar)}{ਠੋਕਰ (ṭhokar)}]{\pa{ਠੋਕਰ} (ṭhokar) — a stumble}

\label{lesson:PA-C310-thokar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to die, then the Punjabi for to slip.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਠੋਕਰ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਠੋਕਰ}} — \emph{ṭhokar} — \textquotedblleft{}a stumble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਹਨੇਰੇ} \pa{ਵਿੱਚ} \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਇੱਕ} \pa{ਪੱਥਰ} \pa{ਨਾਲ} \pa{ਠੋਕਰ} \pa{ਖਾਧੀ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hanere vich maiṁ ikk patthar nāl ṭhokar khādhī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the dark I stumbled over a stone.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਠੋਕਰ}} (\emph{ṭhokar}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*ṭhokk}, \textquotedblleft{}knock\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{ṭhokar}, \textquotedblleft{}blow\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 5513). Its use for a stumble is not given there.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhokar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhokar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hanere vich maiṁ ikk patthar nāl ṭhokar khādhī.} — In the dark I stumbled over a stone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for to die, then the Punjabi for to slip, then say \emph{ṭhokar} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਠੋਕਰ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਟੁੱਟਣਾ} (ṭuṭṭṇā)}{ਟੁੱਟਣਾ (ṭuṭṭṇā)}]{\pa{ਟੁੱਟਣਾ} (ṭuṭṭṇā) — to get broken}

\label{lesson:PA-C310-tuttna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to slip, then the Punjabi for a stumble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਟੁੱਟਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਟੁੱਟਣਾ}} — \emph{ṭuṭṭṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get broken\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮੇਰਾ} \pa{ਗਲਾਸ} \pa{ਫ਼ਰਸ਼} \pa{ਉੱਤੇ} \pa{ਡਿੱਗਿਆ} \pa{ਅਤੇ} \pa{ਟੁੱਟਿਆ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā galās farsh utte ḍiggiā ate ṭuṭṭiā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My glass fell on the floor and broke.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \pa{ਉਹ} \pa{ਸ਼ੀਸ਼ਾ} \pa{ਟੁੱਟਿਆ}, \emph{oh shīshā ṭuṭṭiā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਟੁੱਟਣਾ}} (\emph{ṭuṭṭṇā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{truṭyati}, \textquotedblleft{}is broken, falls asunder\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{ṭuṭṭṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}is broken\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 6065).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਤੋੜਨਾ} (toṛnā)}{ਤੋੜਨਾ (toṛnā)}]{\pa{ਤੋੜਨਾ} (toṛnā) — to break something}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a stumble, then the Punjabi for to get broken.

\textbf{\pa{ਤੋੜਨਾ}} — \emph{toṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to break something\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਣਾ} (ḍullhṇā)}{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਣਾ (ḍullhṇā)}]{\pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਣਾ} (ḍullhṇā) — to get spilt}

\label{lesson:PA-C310-dullhna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to get broken, then the Punjabi for to break something.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਣਾ}} — \emph{ḍullhṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get spilt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਫ਼ਰਸ਼} \pa{ਉੱਤੇ} \pa{ਮੇਰਾ} \pa{ਦੁੱਧ} \pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਿਆ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{farsh utte merā dudh ḍullhiā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My milk spilt on the floor.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \pa{ਉਹ} \pa{ਪਾਣੀ} \pa{ਕਮਰੇ} \pa{ਵਿੱਚ} \pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਿਆ}, \emph{oh pāṇī kamre vich ḍullhiā}.

\textbf{\pa{ਡੁੱਲ੍ਹਣਾ}} (\emph{ḍullhṇā}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*ḍhulati}, \textquotedblleft{}bends, falls, flows\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{ḍullhaṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be poured out\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 5593).
